name: Raymond James Financial
description: Raymond James is mainly a wealth-management firm: about 72 percent of its segment revenue comes from its Private Client Group, where 8,943 advisors look after $1.67 trillion of client assets, about 60 percent of it in fee-based accounts charging a percentage of assets. It also runs a Capital Markets arm (investment banking and brokerage), an Asset Management segment (fees on managed programmes and its own funds), and a Bank segment (Raymond James Bank and TriState Capital Bank) that lends to clients and corporates and earns net interest on $65.3 billion of assets. The bank and client cash balances give it interest-rate sensitivity that pure brokers without a bank lack, and because it lets advisors affiliate as employees, independent contractors or via its RIA custody arm, advisor payouts are the biggest cost (compensation ratio 64.5 percent). Fiscal year ends September 30.

employees.note: Approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) plus 5,065 independent contractor advisors; 8,943 financial advisors in all (employee and independent contractor) in the PCG segment.

businessLines.name: Private Client Group
businessLines.how: Clients pay advisory fees, mainly a percentage of assets in fee-based accounts ($1,008B, 60.5 percent of $1,666.5B client assets), plus brokerage commissions and product and account-service fees; the firm also earns net interest on client cash sweeps. About 57 percent of segment net revenue is paid back to advisors (advisor compensation $5,770M).

businessLines.name: Capital Markets
businessLines.how: Investment banking fees, institutional sales and trading commissions and spreads, equity research, and syndication and management of affordable-housing (tax-credit) funds; results are lumpy with deal flow.

businessLines.name: Asset Management
businessLines.how: Fees set as a percentage of assets under management: on the part of PCG fee-based assets in programmes it oversees (Asset Management Services), on Raymond James Investment Management mutual funds and accounts, plus administrative fees (record-keeping) and trust fees; much of the assets come from PCG clients.

businessLines.name: Bank (Raymond James Bank and TriState Capital Bank)
businessLines.how: Takes FDIC-insured deposits, including sweep cash of broker-dealer clients, and lends (securities-based loans, corporate, real estate and REIT loans, residential mortgages); net interest income is the main revenue. Securities-based and mortgage loans are 46 percent and corporate/tax-exempt loans 33 percent of segment assets of $65.26 billion at 2025-09-30.

businessLines.name: Other (corporate)
businessLines.how: Not a business: corporate costs, interest and private-equity and other investments (net revenues $46M vs $99M in 2024).

brands.name: Raymond James Bank (Florida-chartered state member bank) and TriState Capital Bank (Pennsylvania-chartered state member bank)
brands.note: the Bank segment, $65.26 billion in assets at 2025-09-30; 11.9 percent of segment net revenue before eliminations
